clue.text: Agreement between witches and social worker

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
the ant is the classic social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A pact struck between a witches' group and a social worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding pact or promise.

clue.text: See 4
Entrances to amphitheatre for upper sixth: skip the gold inside

indicators.note: the skip and the gold sit within the school form

parts.note: VI A is a school label for the upper sixth form
to omit is to skip
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A school's upper sixth is told to leave out the gold in an arena.
explanation.walkthrough: Upper sixth is the final year of English secondary school; some schools label it VIA. Vomitoria are the passages that disgorge crowds from a Roman amphitheatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A vomitorium is a passage through which spectators pour in or out of an arena.

clue.text: Pictures of race largely blurred

parts.note: the Grand National is the famous British horse race

indicators.note: the word largely is smeared into a new order

explanation.surface: Photos of a race that are mostly out of focus.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is a famous British steeplechase run at Aintree near Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: London's main art museum, on Trafalgar Square, holds a vast collection of paintings.

clue.text: Newspaper article turning a blind eye?

definitions.text: Newspaper article turning a blind eye?

parts.words: Newspaper article turning a blind eye?
parts.note: a press piece is a ..., and the admiral who put his telescope to his blind eye at Copenhagen gives its owner

explanation.surface: A press article that ignores the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: At Copenhagen in 1801 the admiral famously held the telescope to his blind eye to ignore a signal; his monument stands in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral's monument in London is a tall pillar, also the word for a newspaper feature.

clue.text: Secure house for horse

explanation.surface: Make a stable home safe for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means firm and steady as an adjective, and is also the building where horses are kept.

clue.text: Battle with old-fashioned graft as a quarrel develops

indicators.note: the words grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fight about out-of-date corruption as a row grows.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in two parts: the 1805 naval battle plus 'square' for old-fashioned, naming the London square.
explanation.definitionFit: Trafalgar was Nelson's battle and square means unfashionable; together they name the London plaza.

clue.text: Make height and weight etc

explanation.surface: Make a note of someone's height, weight and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: To build is to construct, and someone's build is their physique or bodily frame.

clue.text: Attitude of agreement or confrontation with lost balls?

indicators.note: the balls are dropped from the phrase

parts.note: an eyeball-to-eyeball meeting is a face-off
both occurrences of ball are removed

explanation.surface: Agreeing or fighting after some balls have gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: To see eye to eye is to agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing eye to eye means sharing the same view.

clue.text: Beast one changed for bird

parts.note: a pig is a farm beast

indicators.note: the word one is altered into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal is swapped for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigeon is a common bird of towns and squares.

clue.text: Setter's in bed for French term

indicators.note: the setter's contraction is placed inside the French bed

parts.note: lit is the French word for bed
the setter speaking says I'm, giving IM

explanation.surface: The compiler is lying in bed during the French academic term.
explanation.definitionFit: A term in the sense of a boundary or end point, as in a time limit.

clue.text: Student opera team is abandoned

parts.note: L is the learner plate, a crossword student
Aida is Verdi's opera
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A student opera company has been dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something by and stop using it is to abandon it for now.

clue.text: Timekeeper came across number in capital

parts.note: to meet someone is to come across them

indicators.note: the abbreviation for number goes inside the city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: Someone keeping time met a number in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A metronome ticks out a steady beat for musicians practising.

clue.text: A mutiny with nothing connected with sound

parts.note: UDI, a unilateral declaration of independence, is a rebellion against a ruling power
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A mutiny that achieved nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: UDI was Rhodesia's 1965 break from British rule, here treated as a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio is an adjective for things concerning recorded or broadcast hearing.

clue.text: Oxford course for the truly celebrated

explanation.surface: An Oxford degree course meant for the famous.
explanation.walkthrough: Greats is the informal name of the Classics degree (Literae Humaniores) at Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Greats is Oxford's Classics course, and great people are those who are famous.

clue.text: Nocturnal sound of Emma's hero

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word that sounds like the name that follows

parts.note: Mr Knightley marries the heroine in Jane Austen's novel Emma

explanation.surface: A night-time noise made by the hero of an Austen novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens every night is nocturnal in its timing.

clue.text: Flesh diet is wrong: here is…

indicators.note: the words are put into the wrong order

explanation.surface: A meat diet is bad for you, says this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link 16 and 17: 'here is… Tours leader' gives the church St Martin-in-the-Fields on Trafalgar Square, ST MARTIN being the patron of Tours.
explanation.definitionFit: The church of the bishop of Tours stands in these open lands of old Westminster.

clue.text: … Tours leader beginning about a mile to home

indicators.note: the start surrounds the mile and the article

parts.note: a beginning is a start
in means at home

explanation.surface: A tour guide starts out about a mile from home.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint Martin was the fourth-century bishop of Tours in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth-century saint was bishop of the French city and its spiritual head.

clue.text: A star, for example, used in riot control

definitions.text: A star, for example, used in riot control

indicators.note: the letters are put to use in a new arrangement

parts.note: EG is short for exempli gratia

explanation.surface: A celebrity is pressed into service by riot police.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas is an irritant spray police use to break up crowds.

clue.text: Tranquil silence envelops the assembly

indicators.note: the hush wraps around the assembly

parts.note: sh calls for silence
a moot is an old gathering or assembly

explanation.surface: A hush descends over the gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth means calm and even, without ripple or disturbance.

clue.text: Make obscure study about old ship

indicators.note: the study goes round the vessel

parts.note: a den is a private study room
Noah's ark is the ancient vessel

explanation.surface: A scholar studies an old ship and makes things murky.
explanation.definitionFit: To darken is to dim or cloud something so it becomes harder to see.

clue.text: Rate of translated wait

parts.note: de is French for of
to wait at table is to serve

explanation.surface: The speed of a waiter rendered into French.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone highly is to judge them worthy, as one who merits reward.

clue.text: Worldwide cover-up intercepted by cast

indicators.note: the throw comes between the letters of the covering
in a down clue the covering is read upwards

parts.note: to lag pipes is to cover them
to lob is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: A cover-up spanning the world is foiled by the actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means extending across the whole planet.

clue.text: A covering, say, should do the trick

indicators.note: the word for the covering is spoken, and a word sounding like it is entered

parts.note: a veil covers the face

explanation.surface: A covering, so they say, ought to do the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or help, to work as needed.

clue.text: Shaft for a river and what to do on it

parts.note: one rows a boat on a river

explanation.surface: A boat pole needed for a river and how to travel on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is the shaft shot from a bow.

clue.text: Sob wildly and peer about one -touching funeral

indicators.note: the word sob is thrown into disorder
the peer goes round the numeral one

parts.note: a peer is an equal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sobbing wildly beside a nobleman at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsequies are funeral rites, so something relating to them is about a burial.

clue.text: Fellows, placed between hills, I won't leave in peace

indicators.note: the fellows sit between one hill and the other

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, and the plural gives two of them
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Men set among hills complain someone will not leave them alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tors are rocky hilltops typical of Dartmoor in southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is one who keeps harassing and pestering a victim.

clue.text: Head librarian's unprepared

indicators.note: 's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

explanation.surface: The chief librarian is caught unready.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'heAD LIBrarian's', so the possessive does the work of 'has' the answer within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad lib means improvised, done off the cuff without rehearsal.

clue.text: Where sea level was calculated afresh at the pole

parts.note: newly means anew, afresh
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A place where mean sea level was worked out once more at the pole.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWLYN is a Cornish fishing port whose tide gauge sets the datum for British map heights.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ordnance Survey's datum of British heights is the mean tide at this Cornish port.

clue.text: Backing for what's genuine about French poetry?

indicators.note: the word for genuine goes round the French poetry

parts.note: real means genuine
vers is the French for verse

explanation.surface: Support for the authentic side of French poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a backing off or turnaround, going into reverse.
